clue.text: Someone who says no — how thick

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who denies, pronounced deny-er
second meaning: the unit measuring the fineness of yarn in stockings and tights, pronounced den-ear

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt the same but said differently, which is the puzzle's running theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A denier denies things, while the denier rating of tights tells you the thickness of the fibre.

clue.text: What about opening with film title?

indicators.note: the exclamation goes around the word for opening

parts.note: eh? is an exclamation meaning what?
a pit is a hole or opening
ET is Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about starting with the name of a film.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive name or byname, a title such as the Great.

clue.text: Usually e-learning is suspect

indicators.note: suspect means dubious, not to be trusted, so the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A sceptic's view that online learning is generally dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: In general is an idiom meaning as a rule or for the most part, the same as usually.

clue.text: Ways to place plug in the middle of prose

indicators.note: place with in tells us to put one word inside the other
with place, signals the plug word going inside
only the inner letters of prose are used, losing its ends

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a plug for a product

explanation.surface: A writer's advice on inserting a product mention mid-text.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads are routes for travel, and way is a common synonym, as in Appian Way.

clue.text: Possibly bent, as a candle might be said to be

definitions.meaning: first meaning: evil, as a bent (crooked) person may be

definitions.text: as a candle might be said to be
definitions.meaning: second meaning: fitted with a wick, said with two syllables in the first sense and one in this

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' is British slang for corrupt or crooked; a candle that has a wick could be called wick'd, said as one syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked means morally bad, like a bent official, and also means having a wick, as candles do.

clue.text: Thoroughly intended — such barbs are accurate

parts.note: well means thoroughly, as in well cooked
aimed means intended, as in aimed to please

explanation.surface: Pointed remarks that hit their target exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-aimed hits its target, so it is precise and on the mark.

clue.text: Twice as many finally in non-religious community

indicators.note: the last letter, the Roman fifty, is swapped for the Roman hundred, twice as many

parts.note: civil means secular, as in a civil wedding

explanation.surface: A secular neighbourhood with double the population.
explanation.walkthrough: L is Roman 50 and C is Roman 100, so the final L becomes C.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic is used attributively for things belonging to a town or its people, as community is in community centre.

clue.text: Stand up before opening

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a wall or fence
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: An instruction to get to your feet ahead of a grand opening.
explanation.definitionFit: An étagère is a piece of furniture with open shelves for displaying ornaments, a kind of stand.

clue.text: Inspired article in "Money"

indicators.note: the article sits inside the slang word for money

parts.note: bread is slang for money
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature on money that motivated someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is literally to breathe in, so inspired is a synonym of breathed in its old physical sense.

clue.text: Ask to remove top? Go ahead!

indicators.note: the top letter of a down answer is its first, which is taken away

parts.note: to plead is to ask earnestly

explanation.surface: Someone asks permission to take off their top and is told to go on.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead is to go in front, ahead of the others.

clue.text: Stylish, wearing wig? Having second thoughts?

indicators.note: the stylish word is dressed in the wig, so it goes inside the word for wig

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig or toupee
in means fashionable, stylish

explanation.surface: Someone dressed smartly in a wig starts to doubt the look.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing is regretting something done, which is to have second thoughts about it.

clue.text: Relax, everyone — don't start to differ

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: tells us the word for differ loses its opening letter

parts.note: deviate means to differ or diverge

explanation.surface: A calming call to a group to stop arguing.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate pain or a rule is to ease it, as when you relax a restriction.

clue.text: Sacked heads can retain a religious profession

indicators.note: sacked suggests being knocked about or plundered, so the following letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Even fired church leaders can keep a statement of their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked heads' reads as dismissed bishops, but sacked is the signal to rearrange; the creed is named after Athanasius of Alexandria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athanasian Creed is a Christian statement of belief, and to profess a creed is a religious profession of faith.

clue.text: Short song about flowery tree — no examples of this round here

definitions.note: plural for a singular answer: the clue jokes that none of these words appear in this grid, which is full of them

indicators.note: the shortened song goes around the rearranged letters
short means the last letter of the song word is cut off

parts.note: a hymn is a religious song

indicators.note: flowery language is elaborate and ornamented, so the letters of tree and no are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: A clipped tune about a blossoming tree, with an aside that such words are rare locally.
explanation.walkthrough: The aside is ironic: DENIER, WICKED, LEAD, BASS, DEFECT and others in this grid are all words of this type.
explanation.definitionFit: A heteronym is a word spelt like another but pronounced differently with another meaning, such as lead the metal and lead the verb.

clue.text: And not the last (but not the first) direction

parts.note: nor means and not

indicators.note: the word last loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A cryptic route description: not the final turning, nor the opening one.
explanation.definitionFit: Northeast is a compass point, a direction halfway between north and east.

clue.text: In magazine we oldies read about Hollywood composer

indicators.note: read about means read the other way round, from right to left
the letters are sitting inside the run of words magazine we oldies

parts.note: the hidden run spans the end of magazine, all of we and the start of oldies

explanation.surface: Old readers find an article on a film-music writer in their magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Loewe wrote the music for My Fair Lady and Gigi, both made into Hollywood films.

clue.text: With difficulty go and clue this dialect

indicators.note: the letters are only brought into the answer by awkward rearrangement

explanation.surface: A setter admits struggling to clue a southern French tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the region is named after the language, langue d'oc, the old tongue of southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Langue d'oc, or Occitan, is the Romance language of southern France, which gave the Languedoc region its name.

clue.text: Transport lobby, maybe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to delight or enchant, stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: a way in, of which a lobby is an example, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.walkthrough: Transport means to carry away with joy here, not a bus or train.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to fill with wonder, and an entrance hall or lobby is where you go into a building.

clue.text: Inhale at start of lecture and speak slowly

parts.note: to draw breath is to inhale

indicators.note: only the opening letter of lecture is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to a nervous lecturer: breathe in and don't rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, lengthened way of speaking, so to drawl is to talk slowly.

clue.text: Foul — a cleaving chop — the pits

indicators.note: the words splitting the chopping tool go into its middle

parts.note: an axe is a tool to chop with
ill means bad, foul

explanation.surface: A nasty chop with an axe leaves things dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pits' looks like slang for something awful, but it is literal: armpits.
explanation.definitionFit: Axillae is the anatomical plural for armpits.

clue.text: Inordinate diatribe about daughter with bare back

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a rant is a bitter verbal attack, a diatribe

indicators.note: back here means the word for bare is turned round

parts.note: nude means bare
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A furious tirade about a daughter seen with an uncovered back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' belongs to the wordplay, turning the word for bare, not to the surface's bare back.
explanation.definitionFit: Redundant means superfluous, more than is needed, which is what inordinate means.

clue.text: A taxi service supported by Waugh?

parts.note: Uber is the ride-hailing taxi firm
on means resting on, supported by; in a down answer it sits below

explanation.surface: A writer named Waugh relying on a cab app.
explanation.walkthrough: Evelyn Waugh is the famous one; the question mark points to his son.
explanation.definitionFit: Auberon Waugh was a journalist and novelist, son of Evelyn, so he is one example of a Waugh.

clue.text: UK record label's coverage in Canada

parts.note: British means of the United Kingdom
Columbia is a famous record label

explanation.surface: A British record company's distribution reach across Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: British Columbia is a Canadian province, an area covered within the country.

clue.text: Broadcast vulgar singer

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so we use how a word sounds

parts.note: base means low and vulgar

explanation.surface: An offensive vocalist on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The low singer is spelt like the fish but said like base, another heteronym.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a male singer with the lowest voice range.

clue.text: At first Edward follows endless country music

indicators.note: the initial of Edward comes after the shortened country
the country loses its last letter

parts.note: India is a country

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Edward is used

explanation.surface: Edward's turn comes after a boundless country-music set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country music' looks like a genre to name; country is India and music alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie is a genre of music from independent labels.

clue.text: A haven in Monaco, as I suspected

indicators.note: the letters are sitting inside the following run of words

parts.note: the run starts with the last letter of Monaco and ends with the first of suspected

explanation.surface: Monaco turns out to be the tax haven we suspected.

clue.text: Speaks about a youth ultimately untrained — in these?

definitions.text: Speaks about a youth ultimately untrained — in these?

indicators.note: the word for speaks wraps around the other letters

parts.note: says means speaks
a lad is a youth

indicators.note: only the final letter of untrained is taken

explanation.surface: Describing an inexperienced young man and asking when such greenness happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad days are the time of youthful inexperience, when a young lad is still untrained.

clue.text: Door half-centred initially in Corinthian order of architecture

indicators.note: the doubled centre of door is cut to half its size, one letter instead of two

parts.note: the word is used as written before one letter is cut

indicators.note: the first letters of in and Corinthian are taken

explanation.surface: A doorway in a classical style, Corinthian being another such order.
explanation.walkthrough: Corinthian looks like part of the definition but only gives its first letter; the answer is a different classical order.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of columns, alongside Ionic and Corinthian.

clue.text: Rebel's imperfection

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to desert one's side, stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: a flaw, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and noun are spelt alike but stressed differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To defect is to abandon your country or party in revolt, and a defect is a fault or flaw.

clue.text: Support alternative

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to back a motion formally
... meaning: another, as in a ... choice or option

explanation.walkthrough: In the sense of being transferred to another post, the verb is stressed on its last syllable, another heteronym.
explanation.definitionFit: Seconding a proposal backs it, and a second opinion is an alternative one.
